fixes.explanation: Right, friend. Job says, “True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.” (Job 12:16) Both are named, so saying only the deceived belong to God doesn't match. The verse doesn't leave out the deceiver.

Robbers is it. Job says, “The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure…” (Job 12:6) Think about how that sounds next to what he said about the righteous man. Job is pointing out that robbers' tents are safe while the righteous man is a laughingstock.

Farmers don't show up in this verse, friend. Job says the tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure (Job 12:6). He puts robbers in those safe tents, and that's why robbers is the answer.

Not quite, friend. Job says the ear tests words, the way the tongue tastes its food (Job 12:11). Passing words along untasted is like boxing up dough nobody sampled. Nothing in the verse says to do that.

Priests show up a few verses later, friend, and not as the answer. Job says wisdom and strength belong to God (Job 12:13). Then he says God leads priests away barefoot (Job 12:19). God is the answer here.

Chains aren't in these verses, friend. Job says God “…leads counselors away barefoot…” and “…leads priests away barefoot…” (Job 12:17, 19). Barefoot is the word he uses, and chains is a different picture.

That's it, friend. Job says, “Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.” (Job 13:3) He wants to speak to God Himself, not just to his friends. I think he wants his answer from the One who actually has it.

Silence, friend. Job says, “If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!” (Job 13:5) He says staying quiet would be their wisdom. It's a sharp line, and I think he means every word.

Right, friend. Job says, “See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.” (Job 13:18) Vindicated means cleared. He has prepared his case, and he says he knows how it will come out.
Not louder, friend. Job says, “Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.” (Job 13:19) He says that if someone can indict him, he will be silent. So the card's statement is False.
